blind.description: A stylized medieval wooden windlass or winch. It features a horizontal cylindrical wooden roller drum wrapped in heavy iron chain with a raised central ring attachment, mounted on two sturdy triangular wooden A-frame supports. The frame is reinforced with dark iron corner brackets and bolts, complete with a ratchet gear mechanism. Both ends of the central axle terminate in wooden four-spoked helm-like turning wheels with rounded handles. Surfaces are clean, smooth, solid, and fully textured in warm brown wood and dark grey forged iron.
blind.from_above: A symmetrical mechanical apparatus consisting of a central horizontal wooden drum bound by chain loops, flanked by two parallel timber floor skids at right angles to the drum, with spoked turning wheels extending out from both lateral ends.
blind.height_vs_figure: About 2.5 to 3 feet tall (roughly half the height of the 5 ft 9 in scale figure) and roughly 3.5 to 4 feet wide across the turning handles.
